digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, App. V, App. VI

teaser.en: Its Digo name calls it the guardian of the water pond, and that is exactly where you find it standing.

summary.en: Mrinda ziya is a soft-wooded, aromatic shrub of pond edges and wet hollows. Its Digo name, 'water pond protector', describes where it grows.

about.en: Mrinda ziya is a bushy shrub, usually head-high or a little more, with soft, slightly hairy grey-green leaves that smell strongly when crushed. At the ends of the branches it carries small, crowded flower heads in pink to mauve, typical of the daisy family but without obvious petals. Pakia notes that the Digo recognise it by the look of the whole plant rather than by any single part.

where.en: It grows wherever water collects: around seasonal ponds (ziya), in wet hollows and along ditches and stream margins. It tolerates wet and somewhat salty ground, so it is often one of the few shrubs standing in a pond basin after the water has dried back.

culture.en: The name is a small description of the landscape. Pakia uses it as an example of how Digo plant names mark habitat: species of freshwater ponds carry the affix ziya, as in Mrinda ziya and Ndago ziya, the nutgrass of wet places.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name Mrinda ziya and explains it as 'water pond protector', because the shrub is so commonly found near ponds. No other Mijikenda or Swahili name is recorded for it. In English it is called marsh fleabane; its scientific name is Pluchea dioscoridis.

reason.en: Another Pluchea shrub, named for fishing
Named for its liking for water
